idiom_name: match over envelope metadata into HashMap<RouteKey, mpsc::Sender<Envelope>>
implementation_notes: The router is a task: one mpsc::Receiver for the input, one Sender per destination, and a match that maps envelope metadata to a route. Bounded channels give backpressure, the routing function is pure and testable, and no broker or framework is involved. Choose it for in-process flows and for tests of routing rules; the route table lives in the process, so reconfiguration means a message or a restart.
pitfalls: An accidentally dropped Sender terminates its route silently (recv yields None).
Unbounded channels remove backpressure and turn overload into memory growth.

variants.name: Broker-side routing with lapin (RabbitMQ)
variants.idiom_name: lapin basic_publish with a routing key + exchange kind + queue bindings
variants.implementation_notes: The routing table moves into the broker: declare an exchange with an ExchangeKind (topic/direct/fanout/headers), publish with a routing key derived from message metadata, and let queue bindings select the destinations - the process then only produces and consumes. Choose it when the rule table must be editable at runtime or shared between services, since bindings can be changed without redeploying producers; deliveries must be acked explicitly and auto-recovery should be enabled.
pitfalls: Without enable_auto_recover the router stops consuming (and stops publishing topology) after a broker restart.
A routing key matching no binding is dropped by the broker; alternate exchanges or a mandatory flag make the miss visible.
An unacked delivery after a consumer crash is redelivered, so consumers must be idempotent.
